programs.title: The Wild Sides
programs.desc:
The creators of the three-part series follow the fate of several families of wild animals living in the Mashatu reserve in Botswana.The production was created over two years and presents the fate of four species.Around the bed of the dried river there are a pride of lions, elephants, a leopard, jackals with offspring, and playful baboons.Every day, these creatures fight to survive and raise their offspring in difficult conditions, and their fates are inextricably linked.Macquele the leopard is a single mother who must deal with the presence of hyenas, lions and jackals, as well as a troop of baboons giving her away her position every time she hunts.A herd of elephants led by Ukwethemba searches for food and water, covering long distances.For the young Abancane elephant, life on the move is not easy.Jackals are monogamous.The male and female of this species raise their offspring together.To find food for them, they must face much larger predators.Baboons are smart, cunning and cause trouble wherever they go.Among them are Umusa and her son
The creators of the three-part documentary follow the adventures of the inhabitants of the Mashatu reserve in Botswana, which is a wildlife enclave.The heroes of this action-packed story are families of leopards, elephants, jackals and baboons.They lead different lifestyles and have different survival strategies, but their fates are closely intertwined.The cameras captured scenes of carefree play of the young ones, as well as tense moments when the animals' lives were at stake.For two years, the filmmakers observed the challenges posed to the fauna by the extreme weather conditions prevailing in this part of Africa.Survive the drought The first part of the documentary story focuses on the fight for survival while waiting for rain.One of the heroines is Macquele the leopard, who raises her daughter alone.The problem for her is not only the lack of water and food, but also the threat from hyenas, lions and jackals.Drought is also deadly for elephants, which are said to have no natural enemies in the animal world.However, they use their own methods to reach the water.Thanks to them, other species also increase their chance of survival.The filmmakers also observe conflicts in a troop of baboons.It turns out that these smart and cunning monkeys often get themselves into trouble.

programs.title: Savage Kingdom
programs.desc: The Savute region, which is located in Botswana, can be both a benevolent paradise and an extremely brutal hell for animals.However, it will always be unpredictable.Covering an area of ​​three thousand square miles, the African savannah is home to competing clans of predators.The survival of lions, leopards, hyenas and wild deer depends on huge herds of their potential prey - buffaloes, elephants and zebras.Every day means a fight for survival, in which the law of nature is the most important.The series has six episodes, thanks to which viewers will be transported to the extraordinary world of animals.There, death can come without warning.Even the most powerful and seemingly invincible kings of the savannah do not know when their last day will come.Viewers will also see how changing weather conditions affect the carnivore clans.During the rainy season, young are born, drought means less food and a dramatic struggle for survival.

programs.title: Into The Okavango
programs.desc: The Okavango Basin is a source of life-giving water for approximately one million people.Animals also draw from this spring - the world's largest population of African elephants, herds of lions, cheetahs and birds.However, this idyllic land is under threat due to human activities.The film is a documentary record of an expedition whose participants try to save the river system that feeds one of the last wild and naturally beautiful corners of the Earth - the Okavango Delta.The four-month expedition led through three countries, and the researchers defending this area covered nearly 2.5 thousand kilometers.km.

programs.title: Predator Fails
programs.desc: Lions, panthers and other predators arouse admiration as reliable hunters.However, hunting down prey requires a lot of effort from them.Very often, their search for prey ends in failure, which means hunger.Viewers will see how the most famous hunters in the animal world cope.They will learn how strength, speed, strategy and teamwork make predators successful in chasing, fighting and killing.They will see the difference between ocean hunters and forest hunters and savannah kings.The creators of the series show how poisonous venom, sharp claws and huge mouths are used.They also present survival strategies for potential victims, who often manage to escape the predator.

programs.title: America The Beautiful: Wild South West
programs.sub_title: On the edge of the desert
programs.desc: There is a 146-kilometer area between California's Death Valley and Mount Whitney, the highest peak in California.The authors of the program travel through deserts, mountains and wetlands with their cameras.
